title: Research: certify terminal X/Y readout kernels for selected centre errors
body:
PR2622's complete projected endpoint detects every centre-output error, but its open question asks which weakened readouts admit cancellation. This certifies the two terminal stream halves of the same selected 144-call schedule:

| Final readout | Exact rank | Kernel dimension |
|---|---:|---:|
| All 14,336 ordinary owners | 1,152 | 0 |
| X only, 7,168 owners | 1,024 | 128 |
| Y only, 7,168 owners | 1,003 | 149 |

Each half has 128 individually invisible sites. Y also has 21 dependencies among individually visible error columns. The complete kernel bases, square minors and exact witnesses are retained. In particular, errors `-4*e8 + e40` cancel on every final Y owner while leaving 111 X owners nonzero. A half-readout therefore loses a concrete complementary restoration obligation; this is not a legal centre replacement.

Only `research/selected-centre-stream-readouts/` is added. A new reverse-adjoint implementation independently reproduces **every** local/global response coefficient from ywz65's PR2622, then computes the new quotients. Exact rational kernel vectors give upper rank bounds; separately computed nonzero prime-field minors give matching lower bounds. Two literal forward witness replays each retain all 2,835,792 scalar instructions, 144 paired bridges, shared helpers, clears and 16 signed terminal exchanges. No predecessor code is imported; its byte-exact comparison receipt is source-pinned with credit.

Validation on Windows x64, standard-library **CPython 3.12.10**:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/selected-centre-stream-readouts
```

The registered replay and all three test groups pass, including assignment-adjoint basis checks, 96 permutation-sum determinant oracles, bridge-sign and duplicate-column controls, optimized Git-free read-only replay, archive/reference corruption, bool/int receipt substitution and occupied-output refusal. Metadata/source pins and `git diff --check` pass. TEMP/TMP were directed to a writable directory for the restricted Windows export fixtures.

This is a **common-frame scalar projection**: native frame/idle/address actions remain identity. Native covariance, an actual caller accepting the quotient, complementary-output consumption/restoration, physical movement/hosting/precision, full supplier admission and all-size/formal obligations remain open. No changed paid profile, recursive-call floor, supplier or kappa is claimed. Hosted CI and independent human/subagent review are unrun.

Started from canonical main `b017900dbb94d81afec343924c1a7fa6d540a7db`, priority revision 5, and rebased onto freshly checked `f1a0b38b7189ad9dcff29671e318c657fbaed862`. Guidance, selected record and scientific inputs are byte-identical. Final live overlap retained all metadata matches across 722 open PRs and 1,436 Discussion records with complete pagination and no warnings; relevant dependency heads are unchanged. This does not search arbitrary diffs or prove novelty. [Canonical claim/result: Discussion2791](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2791). TASK.json records the selection, explicit scope change, evidence and bounded stopping decision.

Credit **ywz65 / PR2622** (`4ffb893a08e8868057a30a065642d0b5f647f742`) for the full response and weakened-readout question; **PR2763** (`24b985e05d77a6005e3b18cdd4a7c33da9c0d260`) separately audits source histories and excludes this response claim; **Sagar Thakrar / PR2199**, **Adam Gall / PR1918**, **commdata2338 / PR2048**, **Aaron Wang / PR2391**, and the retained Rohan Arun/Jeremy Kothe/Hao Yan/icekylinx/DreamingOfClouds/Douglas Colkitt construction and compiler lineage. New calculation, proof and code by **Arham Tahir with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance**. Apache-2.0. The finite two-readout task stops here; further construction needs a legal caller and complete budget.
